limits.when: The effective ordinary t scale tends to zero at an attainable concentration point.
limits.detect: A reachable concentration point has multiplicity $k$, with $k=\nu(n-k)$ for held shape; use the limiting value two for free shape. Equality is unresolved.

limits.name: right translated half-family
limits.when: The skew $\xi$ tends to infinity, with endpoint and one-sided scale chosen to retain any held mean and standard deviation.
limits.detect: The numerically compared half-family face wins among retained candidates while satisfying held constraints.

limits.name: left translated half-family
limits.when: The skew $\xi$ tends to zero, with endpoint and one-sided scale chosen to retain any held mean and standard deviation.
limits.detect: The numerically compared half-family face wins among retained candidates while satisfying held constraints.

limits.name: tie collapse

limits.detect: A reachable concentration point has multiplicity $k>\nu(n-k)$ for held shape; for free shape the diagnosed threshold is $k>2(n-k)$.

limits.name: scale collapse

limits.message: Likelihood is unbounded at a tie

limits.name: symmetric scale-collapse equality
limits.when: Held xi is one and the standard deviation tends to zero at the held mean.
limits.detect: The tie multiplicity satisfies $k=\nu(n-k)$; the inverse-scale likelihood is strictly increasing to a finite unattained supremum.

limits.name: nonunit-skew scale-collapse equality
limits.when: Held xi differs from one and the standard deviation tends to zero at the held mean.
limits.detect: The tie multiplicity satisfies $k=\nu(n-k)$; the finite/face likelihood comparison is unresolved.

limits.name: reflected translated half-normal

limits.detect: The numerically compared limiting face is selected over the retained finite candidates.

limits.name: translated half-t

limits.detect: The numerically compared limiting face is selected over the retained finite candidates.

limits.name: reflected translated half-t

limits.name: two-piece t with 2 degrees of freedom

limits.detect: The numerically compared limiting face is selected over the retained finite candidates.

limits.name: point mass
limits.when: Scale satisfies $\sigma\to0$ with the latent normal centre inside one observed cell.
limits.detect: Both coefficients are free and all observations are equal.

limits.name: shifted Bernoulli
limits.when: Scale satisfies $\sigma\to0$ and location approaches the shared boundary of two adjacent cells at a rate that preserves their observed proportions.
limits.detect: Both coefficients are free and the integer sample range is one.

limits.name: zero-scale limit
limits.when: Scale satisfies $\sigma\to0$ with location fixed.
limits.detect: Location is held and every observed cell closure $[x_i,x_i+1]$ contains that location.

limits.name: point mass collapse
limits.when: Scale satisfies $\sigma\to0$ as location approaches a value occurring exactly half the time.
limits.detect: A value occurs exactly half the time, and its collapse log likelihood is at least the best numerically found interior log likelihood minus $10^{-8}n$. With location held at that value, the collapse supremum is always unattained.

limits.when: the size $r$ tends to infinity and $p$ tends to one with $r(1-p)/p=\bar x>0$ fixed
limits.detect: both coefficients are free, $\bar x>0$, and $S^2=n^{-1}\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)^2\le\bar x$

limits.name: scale collapse
limits.when: The free scale $\sigma$ tends to zero at a location occupied by observations.
limits.detect: With held location $\mu$, held negative shape $\lambda$, and free scale, the tie count $k$ satisfies $(n-k)/|\lambda|-k=0$. Other collapse configurations may be unbounded or rejected by the default tie guard.

limits.name: infeasible held support
limits.when: The held scale $\sigma$ and positive shape $\lambda$ leave no positive-likelihood support containing the sample.
limits.detect: The smallest radius about an eligible location containing the data exceeds $\sigma/\lambda$, or equals it when $0<\lambda<1$ and endpoint density is zero.

limits.name: unbounded likelihood
limits.when: A free power $\gamma$ tends to infinity while the other free coefficients concentrate the excess distribution at its common observed value.
limits.detect: With threshold held, the excesses are constant and the held coefficients permit concentration. In particular, this occurs with both shapes and scale free.

limits.when: The shape $\alpha$ tends to infinity with $\gamma$ fixed and $\sigma\alpha^{-1/\gamma}$ fixed at a positive scale.
limits.detect: With all regular coefficients free, the Burr certificate selects this face. Held power uses the certified Lomax comparison; held scale with both shapes free uses a strictly concave scalar certificate.
limits.name: shifted weibull; subtract min before fitting

limits.when: The power $\gamma$ tends to infinity with $\alpha\gamma$ fixed at a positive tail exponent and $\sigma$ fixed.
limits.detect: With all regular coefficients free, the Burr certificate selects this face. Held power uses the certified Lomax comparison; held scale with both shapes free uses a strictly concave scalar certificate.
limits.name: shifted pareto; subtract min before fitting

limits.when: The power $\gamma$ tends to infinity with $\alpha\gamma$ fixed at a positive tail exponent and $\sigma$ fixed.
limits.detect: Scale and threshold are held, both shapes are free, and every excess is at least $\sigma$. If all excesses equal $\sigma$, the likelihood is instead unbounded.
limits.name: shifted Pareto with its endpoint held at min + scale

With shape2 held at one, shape1 diverges and scale vanishes at fixed product.

limits.name: positive log-variance
limits.when: Both free shapes $p$ and $q$ tend to infinity with their ratio and scale chosen to concentrate at the common observation.
limits.detect: All observations are equal and both shapes are free.

limits.when: With $p$ held, $q$ and $b$ tend to infinity while $b/q$ tends to a positive gamma scale.
limits.detect: Constant data select this limit analytically; nonconstant data require the signed gamma-tail and interior profile certificate. Unresolved comparisons stop.

limits.when: With $q$ held, $p$ tends to infinity and $b$ tends to zero while $bp$ tends to a positive inverse-gamma scale.
limits.detect: Constant data select this limit analytically; nonconstant data use the reciprocal signed gamma-tail and interior certificate. Unresolved comparisons stop.

limits.when: The shape $q$ tends to infinity while $p$ tends to a positive finite shape and $b/q$ tends to a positive gamma scale.
limits.detect: The signed joint gamma tail and compact interior cover exclude finite competitors; likelihood bounds separate this face from the inverse-gamma face. Unresolved comparisons stop.

limits.when: The shape $p$ tends to infinity while $q$ tends to a positive finite shape and $bp$ tends to a positive inverse-gamma scale.
limits.detect: Reciprocal signed tails and the compact interior cover exclude finite competitors; likelihood bounds separate this face from the gamma face. Unresolved comparisons stop.

limits.name: half-normal with the same endpoint; use mlhnorm(x, mu = 0) after a held translation, or mlhnorm(x, mu = NULL) with a free one

limits.name: unbounded scale collapse
limits.when: The free scale $\sigma$ tends to zero at the free or held endpoint.
limits.detect: With held shape, $k>\nu(n-k)$ endpoint observations cause collapse. With free shape and a held endpoint, any endpoint tie suffices. With both endpoint and shape free, $2k>n$ suffices under the fitting restriction.

limits.name: finite unattained scale-zero supremum
limits.when: The free scale $\sigma$ tends to zero at fixed positive shape.
limits.detect: The endpoint multiplicity satisfies $k=\nu(n-k)$ in a sample of size $n$. The scale supremum is finite and unattained.

limits.name: degenerate
limits.when: As $N\to\infty$ with positive $K$ and $n$ held, the law tends to a point mass at zero.
limits.detect: All observations are zero, only $N$ is free, and the held counts $K$ and $n$ are positive.
